name: Hanalani Schools Holiday Craft Fair
schedule_text: Saturday, November 14, 2026, 9 AM-2 PM.
description: Central Oʻahu school craft and food fair, free to shoppers.
notes: A KITV roundup showed Hanalani also ran a Spring Craft Fair on April 25, 2026 with 60+ crafters and food vendors. No 2027 spring date found yet. Different from the Mililani Town Association Holiday Craft Fair on your skip list.

name: HUOA Winter Craft and Gift Fair
schedule_text: Saturday, November 28, 2026; one listing also shows a second day on Sunday, November 29. Hours not stated.
description: Annual cultural craft and gift fair bringing together the Okinawan community and craft shoppers in Waipahu each November.
notes: The source lists Nov 28-29 in one entry and Nov 28 only in another. I included only the date both entries share. Food vendors are not confirmed. Check HUOA's own page.

name: McKinley High School Band & Orchestra Winter Craft & Gift Fair
schedule_text: Listed for December 2026 with the date still to be confirmed.
description: Winter craft and gift fair listed on a Waikīkī-focused events calendar.
notes: Title-only listing. The organizer is inferred from the event name. Venue (presumably McKinley High School) and date not confirmed. Food vendors are not mentioned.

name: Mililani High School Holiday Food & Craft Fair
schedule_text: Listed for Saturday, November 21, 2026. Hours not stated.
description: Holiday food and craft fair listed on a Waikīkī-focused events calendar.
notes: Calendar title only. Venue, organizer and hours not given. It may overlap with the Mililani Town Association Holiday Craft Fair on your skip list, so check for duplication.

name: Ahiki Acres produce pre-order pickup
schedule_text: Pre-order online; pickup Sundays 10:30 am-4:30 pm at ʻAi Love Nalo (pre-order required). Also at Kailua Town Farmers' Market Sundays 8 am-12 pm. The online marketplace is updated Thursday afternoons.
description: Small Native Hawaiian-owned vegetable farm in Waimānalo that sells weekly pre-ordered produce for pickup.
notes: This is a pre-order marketplace, not a fixed-share CSA; the farm ran a prepaid CSA in 2019. Sierra Club Oʻahu also lists farm pickup Fridays 12-2 pm and Waimānalo Co-Op and Health Center Wednesday pickups, but that is older third-party info. The Instagram handle is from a CTAHR farm profile listing Ahiki Acres.

name: Asagi Hatchery (fresh eggs and produce storefront)
schedule_text: The hatchery's own contact page lists store hours of Monday to Friday 8am-5pm and Saturday 9am-noon.
description: Kalihi chicken hatchery and supply store, in business since 1935. A directory listing says it sells fresh eggs from Peterson Upland Farm and Kaʻu coffee. In 2017 Roots (Kokua Kalihi Valley) set up a small produce storefront inside it.
source_label: Asagi Hatchery website (contact page); Roots Kalihi blog (2017); hawaiianlocal.com directory
notes: Primarily a hatchery and supply store, so it is a stretch as an egg stand. The contact page is undated. Other non-review directories list different hours (for example Mon-Thu 9-3, Fri 9-1). Phone: (808) 845-4522. Per a 2017 Roots post the produce storefront was open Mon-Fri 8am-5pm and Sat 9am-noon; whether it still exists is unconfirmed. Peterson Upland Farm closed in 2024 per Honolulu Magazine, so egg sourcing may have changed.

name: Da Banana Stand (Living Circle Farms Hawaii)
schedule_text: Open seasonally and by appointment only.
description: Seasonal produce and natural products grown on the farm and sold at Da Banana Stand.
notes: Page is undated. Appointment-only, so it may not be a walk-up roadside stand. No hours or contact method retrieved.

name: De La Mesa Farms CSA boxes
schedule_text: CSA boxes with pickup locations on the Windward side and in Honolulu.
description: Farm offering CSA boxes with Windward and Honolulu pickup sites.
source_label: Community article (Sierra Club Oʻahu Group resource list)
notes: Only a single undated third-party mention. The Instagram handle comes from that list and was not tied to a farm page.

name: Eggs Hawaii / Ka Lei Eggs
organizer: Eggs Hawaii (Ka Lei Eggs / Hawaiian Maid Eggs)
description: Egg outlet in Kalihi selling Ka Lei eggs from the family's Waiʻanae Valley farm. Eggs are sold by the tray, with a menu of grades and sizes on the wall.
source_label: Onolicious Hawaiʻi (blog); Eggs Hawaii family-farm page; Star-Advertiser via Yahoo News
notes: This is a staffed retail egg shop, not a roadside or honor stand. Hours are not stated in the sources I could use. The Star-Advertiser piece says lines formed in 2025 at a Kalihi shop it calls Island Fresh Eggs, which sells eggs from a Waiʻanae farm; I did not confirm it is the same business. Honolulu Magazine (March 2025 update) says Ka Lei eggs are also sold at Kakaʻako Farmers Market, which is already in your directory.

name: Farm Link Hawaiʻi (local produce boxes, delivery and Kalihi hub pickup)
venue_name: Farm Link Kalihi Hub (food hub / warehouse)
schedule_text: Pickup at the Kalihi hub 10 am-3:30 pm, six days a week (Wed-Mon, closed Tuesday). Delivery windows 9 am-5 pm on most days, with next-day delivery when you check out by midnight.
admission: Free pickup with no order minimum; delivery has a $50 order minimum and an $11.99 fee, waived for Farm Link Members and EBT/SNAP households.
description: Online local-grocery aggregator that sources from Oʻahu farms, ranchers and bakers and delivers islandwide or offers hub pickup. Honolulu Magazine (2020) described a $30 CSA produce box assembled from its farms.
notes: The site says no subscription is required, so this is order-by-order rather than a fixed-box CSA. Whether the $30 CSA box still exists was not confirmed. The Kalihi street address was not stated in the pages I saw.

name: Frankie's Nursery Fruit Stand
schedule_text: Tuesday to Saturday, 9:00am to 3:00pm. Closed Sunday and Monday.
description: Fruit stand at a tropical fruit-tree nursery selling fruit harvested daily from mature trees plus homemade tropical juices. Fruit varies by season; the site gives mangoes as primarily a summer fruit and durians as a winter fruit. Visitors can walk the nursery grounds, where the fruit trees are for sale.
notes: Own page, but it carries no update date (footer shows 2022), so current hours should be confirmed. The site shows an Instagram link but no handle, so instagram is null.

name: Haleiwa Fruit Shack
schedule_text: Usually open daily, 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. The stand's own TikTok says it is open 7 days a week 'most of the time'. A TikTok post also says it sells at the KCC Farmers Market on Saturdays, 7:30–11:15 a.m.
description: Roadside fruit shack selling fruit platters, fresh-pressed sugarcane juice and cold coconuts.
source_label: Business Facebook page; hours from nateeatshawaii.com listing and the business's TikTok (@thehaleiwafruitshack)
notes: No Instagram handle was confirmed, so it is null. The TikTok handle is @thehaleiwafruitshack. The address is the same on the Facebook page and several listings, but one TikTok caption shows a different number (62-540), so verify. Hours may vary day to day.

name: Ho Farms produce pickup (Ewa Beach / Honolulu)
venue_name: Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach); Republik (Honolulu)
schedule_text: Pickup Mondays 3-5 pm on Old Fort Weaver Road (Ewa Beach) and Saturdays 1-3 pm at Republik (Concert and Event Center), Honolulu. Farm is in Kahuku.
description: Kahuku farm listed with island pickup locations for online produce orders.
source_label: Community article (Sierra Club Oʻahu Group resource list)
notes: Undated third-party list, and it's unclear whether a subscription or box is offered. Verify on the farm's own site.

name: ʻĀINA Farm Stand
venue_name: Kōkua Learning Farm (Unit B on the highway, with Kōkua General Store)
schedule_text: Tuesday to Friday 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.; Saturday opens 8:30 a.m. (Saturday closing time not stated in the source).
description: Stand opened November 2024 in the property's historic flower shop. Sells produce from the Kōkua Learning Farm and other local farms plus value-added products. Proceeds go to the foundation.
source_label: Community article (Oahu Travel Guide), indexed about 4 days before 2026-10-31
notes: Third-party source; the organizer's own page was not retrieved. Haleʻiwa is outside the listed towns (Waiʻanae, Nanakuli, Kunia, Wahiawā, Waialua).

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand
neighborhood: Kahuku (across from Kawela Bay, near Turtle Bay Resort)
description: Roadside stands selling local pineapple, coconut, sugarcane, mango and banana bread. The 2026 North Shore guide lists the address and says cash is preferred.
source_label: Wanderlustyle North Shore eating guide (2026), with older descriptions from Lonely Planet and a YAH Global directory
notes: No posted days or hours were found. This is a cluster of stands across from Kawela Bay and may overlap with stands already in the directory (e.g., Chue's Farm Fruit Stand). Check for duplicates before adding. A Hawaiʻi Life guide's 9–5 daily hours appear to refer to Kahuku Farms, so I did not use them.

name: Kahuku Land Farms Stand (Kahuku fruit stands)
schedule_text: 2017 Star-Advertiser: open daily during daylight hours.
description: Collective of roadside fruit stands on Kamehameha Hwy, mauka side, across from the Kawela Bay entrance just past Turtle Bay Resort on the way toward Haleiwa. Sells bags of cut fruit, whole fruit, some vegetables, and cut coconuts. Much of the fruit is grown on farms just behind the stands.
notes: Sources are old. A Hawaii Life blog post (https://www.hawaiilife.com/blog/kahuku-land-farms-fruit-stands-new-rules/) says conservation-easement rules for the surrounding land could change how the stands operate. A recent Hawaii Life guide lists 'Kahuku Fruit Stands' as a permanent structure tied to Kahuku Farms, open daily 9am to 5pm. That conflicts with the independent-stand description, and Kahuku Farms is already in the directory. A recent TikTok caption (updated 2026-10-26) also mentions a 'Kahuku Fruit Stand', so it appears to still operate, but the exact operator and current hours are unverified. No street address was stated in a usable source.

name: Kahumana Organic Farms CSA
schedule_text: Weekly or bi-weekly half- or full-share produce box, with pickup or doorstep delivery chosen at signup (per Honolulu Magazine description of the site's ordering flow). Pickup locations around the island.
description: Certified organic 25-acre farm in Lualualei Valley offering CSA produce and meal boxes with island pickup sites, plus a Farm Hub fruit box sold through Oahu Fresh.
notes: Same organization as the existing Kahumana Organic Farms Farm Market entry; this is the CSA program. Current prices and pickup sites were not on the pages I saw. Slow Food Oahu (undated, roughly 2024) lists $30-$32 per box with 13 pickup sites. The site also advertises free summer Kaukau 4 Keiki produce boxes for eligible keiki, which is a separate program.

name: Kualoa Coconut Man
schedule_text: Daily, 9:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
description: Simple roadside stand on Kamehameha Highway selling fresh coconuts opened on the spot, plus fruit such as bananas and papaya.
source_label: FastFoodClub article, 6 Hawaii Roadside Stands (indexed about 31 days before this research)
notes: The article gives the location only as Kamehameha Highway in Kaneohe, with no street address or hours. A separate aggregator page garbles the address, so I left it null. Verify the exact location and hours before publishing.

name: Let's Grow Farms multi-farm CSA
schedule_text: Weekly bag of seasonal produce. Pickup Saturdays noon-4 pm at Keneke's Grill in Punaluʻu and Sundays 11 am-3 pm at the Waialua Farm Stand. The traditional 6-month prepaid CSA also lists pickup in Hawaiʻi Kai, at Mori by Art & Flea, on-farm in Pearl City, or home delivery.
description: Two-farmer CSA (Dave and Thanh) that grows and packs produce weekly and adds produce from other Oʻahu farms. Has a sliding-scale Food For All program.
notes: Price not on the pages I saw; Slow Food Oahu (undated, roughly 2024) says $20-$25 per bag. The site mentions Instagram and Facebook but gave no handles. Site footer shows Copyright 2026.

name: Local Hawaiian Produce weekly delivery bags
schedule_text: Weekly produce bag delivered on Fridays, with delivery on Oʻahu included.
organizer: Local Hawaiian Produce (Farmer Dave and family)
description: Family farm bagging produce from a Punaluʻu orchard, a Mokuleia organic farm and other trusted organic farmers for weekly delivery.
notes: Price not stated on the page I saw. Page is undated. The Let's Grow Farms site also names a Dave Burlew farming in Punaluʻu; the connection between the two is not confirmed.

name: Local Inside CSA (Hawaii Agricultural Foundation, HAF Ag Park Kunia)
venue_name: HAF Ag Park, Kunia (produce source); pickup sites around Oʻahu
schedule_text: Produce bags with pickup at about a dozen sites across Oʻahu (per HAWAIʻI Magazine; undated).
description: Nonprofit CSA launched in 2015 whose bags are grown by small farmers leasing land at the HAF Ag Park in Kunia.
notes: Sources are old (HAWAIʻI Magazine; Star-Advertiser 2020, which gave localinside.csaware.com and hawaiiagfoundation.org/local-inside). I could not confirm the program is still running; check before publishing.

name: Lohelani Farms CSA
schedule_text: Bi-weekly box of 8-10 items (salad and cooking greens, roots, herbs, seasonal fruit). Delivery for Central Oʻahu residents. Subscribe for one month (2 boxes) or two months (4 boxes).
admission: One month, 2 boxes, delivered to Central Oʻahu: $40. Two months, 4 boxes: $72.
description: Farm CSA delivering a bi-weekly produce box to Central Oʻahu; subscribers sign up by contacting the farm through its website.
notes: Page undated; I could not confirm current availability. The farm's location was not stated in the results.

name: Mahina Pua Farm CSA box
schedule_text: Produce is sold by CSA box, à la carte, or at farmers markets: Kakaʻako Wednesdays, Kaiser HS and Niu Valley Tuesdays, Āina Haina Sundays. CSA pickup times were not stated in the source I used.
description: Urban farm growing vegetables on the east side of Oʻahu and selling by CSA box, à la carte and at four farmers markets.
notes: I'm placing it on the east side based on a listing's 'East side of Oahu' wording; the farm address is not stated. Price and pickup details exist in a LocalHarvest listing, which I did not use. Check the farm's site for current terms.

name: MAʻO Organic Farms CSA
schedule_text: Weekly or every-other-week box with an 8-box commitment. Boxes are delivered to pickup sites across Oʻahu.
description: Organic produce CSA from the Waiʻanae farm and youth-training nonprofit; the 8-box agreement is described as making subscribers co-producers.
notes: The CSA page shows no price or pickup-site list. Older press (2020) cited $32 per box; Slow Food Oahu (roughly 2024) says $32 with 13 pickup sites. Page currency not confirmed.

name: Mohala Farms CSA
schedule_text: Organic produce baskets on Thursdays, with pickup at the farm or in Moʻiliʻili (per Slow Food Oahu; undated).
admission: Per Slow Food Oahu: $25 annual fee, 3-month subscriptions, small basket $20, large basket $30, customizable.
description: Community-initiated organic farm in Waialua with a CSA basket program.
notes: Terms come from a third-party article of unconfirmed date (roughly 2024), not the farm's own page. The Instagram handle comes from the Roots Program Kalihi Valley hub-partner list, which names Mohala Farms in Waialua and links to the same website.

name: North Shore Farm Stand
address: Hale'iwa Road at Paalaa Rd, Haleiwa, HI 96712
schedule_text: Wednesdays 12pm to 6pm per the contact page; the homepage says Wednesdays and Thursdays 12pm to 6pm.
description: Stand selling fresh produce and products from North Shore farmers, homesteaders and entrepreneurs. Farmers listed include Tin Roof Ranch (fruit orchard, chickens, turkeys, sheep) and Ala Mai Farmstead.
notes: Home page says Wed and Thu 12-6pm; contact page lists Wednesdays only. Pages are undated (footer copyright 2024), so confirm hours with the stand. Address is Haleʻiwa but the stand serves the Waialua moku.

name: North Shore Farm Stand (Āina Sustainability Growers of Hawaii)
address: 66-249 Kamehameha Hwy Unit B, Haleiwa, HI 96712
schedule_text: The farm's own site says the stand is open to the public Wednesdays and Thursdays, 12 p.m. to 6 p.m. A Haleʻiwa Town guide lists different hours (Wed–Fri 9 a.m.–3 p.m., Sat 8:30 a.m.–2:30 p.m.), so verify before listing.
organizer: Āina Sustainability Growers of Hawaii LLC (owner and farmer Luis Dasilveira)
description: Farm stand in Haleʻiwa town selling fresh produce and products grown and made in Moku o Waialua.
source_label: Farm's own website; address and alternate hours from haleiwatown.com market guide
notes: The farm's page gives Wed/Thu 12–6 but carries no date. The street address and the conflicting hours come from haleiwatown.com, which calls it the ĀINA Farm Stand. I matched it to this website by name and town. Confirm the schedule with the farm.

name: Oahu Fresh (Farmers' Market Box / subscription delivery)
schedule_text: Weekly or biweekly produce bag delivery or pickup at various island pickup locations; the site mentions weekly Wednesday delivery in one member comment. Order cutoffs apply each week.
admission: Farmers' Market Box $25 (6-7 curated items); Make Your Own Box $30 (6 items); Fruit Box $40 (per site product page).
description: Membership-based produce subscription that has delivered around Oʻahu since 2009, sourcing from a network of local farms and producers. Offers a curated Farmers' Market Box, a build-your-own box and a seasonal fruit box.
notes: Older press (Star-Advertiser 2020, Slow Food Oahu) cites a $15 membership fee; not confirmed on the current site pages I saw. Delivery fees not confirmed on the current site.

name: OK Poultry (farm egg sales)
description: Waimānalo egg farm where customers buy eggs directly at the farm. Onolicious says white and brown eggs are sold in various sizes, and that you need to arrive early because they sell out.
notes: Only a third-party blog post, and an older one, supports this. The street address and current hours appear only on Yelp, which I can't use, so they are null. Verify the address, hours and current status with the farm before publishing. Waimānalo is windward and borderline for your Honolulu/East scope.

name: Red Barn Farmstand
schedule_text: Wednesday through Sunday, 8:00am to 3:00pm (per a Hawaii Life guide).
description: Permanent red-barn farm stand that sells local farmers' produce and island-made goods, with grab-and-go food, coffee and occasional community events. Opened October 2016 on the corner of Kamehameha Hwy and Cane Haul Road.
source_label: Hawaii Life, A Guide to North Shore Oahu Farmers' Markets
notes: I could not open the organizer's own site. Other listings I saw (not used as sources) conflict on hours and appear to mark the business as closed. Confirm it is currently operating before publishing. Phone per the guide: (808) 753-4350.

name: Sun Farm Hawaii (farm produce)
schedule_text: The farm's website lists Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 12 PM as its contact hours. It does not say these are produce-sales hours.
organizer: Marcos and Michele Santos (Sun Farm Hawaii)
description: Family farm in Hawaii Kai growing fruit, vegetables and herbs. A KHON2 report said visitors can stop by the farm to buy locally grown fruit and veggies. The farm also runs garden tours.
source_label: Sun Farm Hawaii website (Our Story / contact info); KHON2 feature on the farm
notes: The address and hours come from the farm's own site. On-farm produce sales come only from an older KHON2 article (khon2.com/local-news/wellness-retreats-yoga-classes-at-sun-farm-hawaii/). Confirm directly that walk-up produce sales are still offered and when. The KHON2 piece also said they sell at local farmers markets.

name: Thrive Family Farm / Thrive Ohana Farm CSA
schedule_text: CSA runs in successive eight-week subscriptions (per Slow Food Oahu; undated).
admission: Per Slow Food Oahu: organic produce $40/week.
description: Small family farm in Haleʻiwa with a CSA component.
notes: Slow Food gives thriveohana.org; the Roots Kalihi Valley hub-partner list gives thriveohana.com and Instagram thrive.hawaii for 'Thrive Ohana Farm' in Haleʻiwa. I could not tie that handle or domain to this exact business, so website and handle are left null.

name: Waiahole Farm
description: Windward-side stand reported to sell fresh-cut fruit, juices and seasonal tropical fruit.
notes: Only a single social mention was found. There is no address, hours or official handle, and I could not tie it to a specific business page. Needs a first-party source before it goes in the directory.

name: Waialua Fresh Egg Farm (farm stand)
description: Family-owned farm selling fresh, cage-free eggs from a roadside stand/trailer. Free parking in front of the stand. A Haleʻiwa Town guide also mentions a bee farm tour.
source_label: Community guide (Haleiwa Town) plus the farm's Facebook page
notes: Sells eggs, not fruit. No stand hours found. The guide was indexed about 323 days before 2026-10-31 and the Facebook page about 216 days. Confirm it is still operating.

name: Waihuena Farm CSA
description: North Shore farm offering CSA membership; interested people email info@waihuenafarm.com.
source_label: Community article (Sierra Club Oʻahu Group resource list)
notes: Only a thin, undated third-party mention; the Instagram handle and email come from that list. Waihuena's own page was not checked.

name: Mahiku Farmers Market
description: Listed by a market aggregator as a weekly market bringing together local growers and food producers in Waimānalo.
notes: Thin aggregator listing with no verified schedule or organizer. Verify that it is active before publishing.

name: Waimanalo Beach Park People's Open Market
schedule_text: Thursday mornings. One listing says 7:15am to 8:15am; another says 7:00am to 8:00am.
description: People's Open Market stop, a program that helps farmers sell off-grade and surplus produce at lower prices. Offers fruits, vegetables and other items not always available in grocery stores. The listing places it on Kalanianaʻole Highway near the baseball fields.
source_label: Soko app market listing; hours cross-checked with vendorsmap.com
notes: Third-party aggregators only, and the hours differ between them. The venue name (Waimanalo Beach Park) comes from vendorsmap.com, and one aggregator's data appears to date from 2015. Confirm with the City's People's Open Market schedule. The organizer is not named in these sources.

name: Waimānalo Farmers Market
schedule_text: Wednesdays, 2:00pm to 5:15pm.
description: Community market on the Windward Coast with seasonal fruits and vegetables and locally made dishes from vendors such as Hawaiian Island Café.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, Your Guide to Farmers Markets on O‘ahu
notes: This is a farmers market rather than a roadside stand, included because it is a recurring Waimānalo produce venue. The Instagram handle (@nalofarmersmarket) is as printed in the magazine guide, which was indexed about 19 days before this research. The organizer is not named in the source.

name: Waimea Valley Farmers Market
schedule_text: Thursdays, 2:00pm to 6:00pm.
description: North Shore weekly farmers market listed in a Hawaii Life guide to North Shore farmers' markets and farm stands.
source_label: Hawaii Life, A Guide to North Shore Oahu Farmers' Markets
notes: Farmers market, not a roadside stand. The guide gave no address or venue in the text I retrieved, so those are null. The guide was indexed about 220 days before this research.

name: Aloha Festivals
venue_name: Royal Hawaiian Hotel Helumoa Gardens and Royal Hawaiian Center (opening); Kalākaua Ave (Hoʻolauleʻa and Floral Parade)
schedule_text: Annual September celebration of Hawaiian culture. The 2026 (80th anniversary) Oʻahu events were: opening ceremony September 5, 4–6pm; the 72nd Waikīkī Hoʻolauleʻa September 19, 6–10pm (vendors from 4pm); and the 78th Floral Parade September 26 at 9am.
description: Hawaiian music, hula, chant and pageantry. It includes a Royal Court investiture, a Waikīkī Hoʻolauleʻa block party with vendors, and a Floral Parade on Kalākaua Ave.
source_label: Third-party event listing (islandsevents.com), cross-checked with alohacalendar.com
notes: Another site (hiestates.com) lists July 10–12, 2026, which conflicts with the September dates. I used the September dates that two sources agree on. I did not find the organizer's own page, so the website is null. 2027 dates were not found.

name: Asia Fest (Year of the Fire Goat Lunar New Year celebration)
schedule_text: February 12-13, 2027. Hours and venue not stated.
description: Billed by the organizer as one of Hawaii's largest Lunar New Year celebrations.
notes: The organizer's page appeared old, but it lists Feb 12-13, 2027. A Honolulu Magazine item described the 2026 inaugural 'Explore Asia Fest' (Feb 28, 2026) with food booths, craft vendors and collectibles; it may be the same series. Venue and vendor mix for 2027 not confirmed.

name: Chinatown 808 Mid-Autumn Festival
schedule_text: Listed on the organizer's events page for September 19, 2026.
description: A Mid-Autumn Festival listed among the Chinatown 808 events.
notes: The organizer's page gives only the name and date. The venue and hours were not found, so I can't say whether food vendors take part.

name: Chinatown Festival & Parade (Lunar New Year)
schedule_text: Annual Lunar New Year festival and parade, listed for January 30, 2027. Start and end times were not found.
description: Chinatown 808 is a volunteer-led nonprofit that runs Honolulu's Chinatown festival and parade for Lunar New Year. The 2026 edition was the 50th, held February 13–14.
notes: Hawaii News Now (Jan 6, 2026) described the 2026 edition. Details for 2027 such as the route and booths were not found.

name: Chinese New Year Celebration (Chinatown Cultural Plaza)
schedule_text: Two-day Lunar New Year festival, Friday and Saturday, January 29–30, 2027. It starts Friday 5pm and runs to 10pm Saturday. A Choy Cheng lion-dance open house through Chinatown is listed 6–9pm.
organizer: Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Hawaiʻi
description: Food booths with traditional Chinese delicacies, vendors selling narcissus flowers, arts and crafts, and live Chinese music and dance. The 2026 edition had more than 40 booths.
source_label: Organizer calendar (Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Hawaiʻi)
notes: The Chamber's calendar also lists the 77th Narcissus Festival Queen Pageant and Coronation Ball. Their exact dates were not captured. Lunar New Year itself is February 6, 2027.

name: Chinese New Year Celebration (Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Hawaii)
schedule_text: Two-day festival, Friday January 29 (from 5 PM) to Saturday January 30, 2027 (to 10 PM).
organizer: Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Hawaii
description: Food booths with traditional Chinese delicacies, vendors selling narcissus flowers, arts and crafts, and live stage performances.
source_label: Chinese Chamber of Commerce of Hawaii event calendar
notes: Organizer calendar page shows 2027 dates, but the page's date metadata looked stale, so re-verify. The 2026 edition (Jan 30-31) had 40+ food, craft and cultural booths. This is separate from the Chinatown 808 Lunar New Year Festival & Parade (ʻAʻala Park), whose 2027 date I did not find.

name: Flores de Mayo & Filipino Fiesta
schedule_text: Every first Saturday of May, 10am–6pm. The 2026 edition (14th Flores de Mayo and 34th Filipino Fiesta) was held May 2.
organizer: Filipino Community Center; the 2024–2026 editions were led by the Filipino Jaycees of Honolulu
description: Oʻahu's largest Filipino cultural celebration, with food, dance and music, a Santacruzan procession, tinikling, a Filipiniana Market and a Sari Sari store. The 2026 contests were a balut eating contest, a purple freeze challenge and Bilao Blitz.
source_label: Organizer website, with Hawaii News Now (April 26, 2026) for the 2026 details
notes: The 10am–6pm hours come from a hawaii-guide.com listing. Hawaii News Now says only 'from 10 a.m.' The street address is not in the sources, only 'Filipino Community Center in Waipahu'.

name: Haleiwa Town Festival
schedule_text: Listed for Saturday, November 14, 2026. Hours not stated.
description: Street festival lined with local artists, merchants, food vendors and entertainers, per an events roundup.
notes: Single aggregator source. Organizer, street and hours not found. The page mixes 2025 and 2026 dates for other events, so confirm with the organizer.

name: Hawaiʻi Food & Wine Festival – Oʻahu weekend
venue_name: Multiple venues, including Sheraton Waikīkī, Halekulani, Alohilani Resort, Hyatt Regency Waikīkī, Kapiʻolani Community College and a Kāneʻohe event
schedule_text: The 16th annual festival ran October 16–November 8, 2026 across three islands. The Oʻahu weekend is November 5–8, 2026.
organizer: Hawaiʻi Ag & Culinary Alliance (festival co-founded by chefs Roy Yamaguchi and Alan Wong)
admission: Ticketed. All Oʻahu events require separately sold tickets.
description: Ticketed chef dinners, wine seminars, grand tastings and a FEAST summit featuring local farmers, ranchers, fishers and chefs. The 2026 theme was 'Traditions and Heritage'.
source_label: Organizer website, with hawaii.com listing for ticketing
notes: This is a ticketed culinary event, not a vendor market. The schedule page I retrieved looked like a cached older-edition page, so I did not use its per-event times.

name: Hawaiʻi FoodieCon & Spring Expo
schedule_text: Listed for February 12–13, 2027.
description: Consumer food convention advertised with over 250 vendors.
notes: The page is an older snapshot but still shows the 2027 date. Confirm hours and ticket prices with Pacific Expos. The organizer's other show listings were ambiguous, so I excluded them.

name: HEART of Honolulu Art Street Festival
schedule_text: Annual; listing expects April 11, 2027, 11 AM-4 PM. Date is described as expected, not confirmed.
description: Annual art street festival in Chinatown with art, live music, food, creative local vendors, cultural performances and maker booths.
notes: Date marked 'expected' and organizer not identified. Confirm with the organizer before listing.

name: Honolulu Festival
venue_name: Hawaiʻi Convention Center (stages also at Ala Moana Center); Grand Parade on Kalākaua Avenue
schedule_text: Annual three-day festival held in March, Friday through Sunday. The 31st edition is March 5–7, 2027.
admission: Free per a third-party listing (festivalnet). A reserved fireworks viewing area at the Royal Hawaiian was offered separately in 2026.
description: Pacific Rim cultural festival with dance and performance stages, art demonstrations, a craft fair, a Japanese product bazaar, a Sake & Food Fest, a parade and Nagaoka fireworks. Performers come from Japan, Korea, Taiwan, the Philippines, Tahiti, Australia and Hawaiʻi.
notes: The organizer says March 5–7, 2027 (Fri–Sun). GoHawaii lists March 6–7, 2027, 10am–4pm. The Honolulu Festival Craft Fair is already in the directory. ASOBIEXPO HAWAII, a sister event, is listed for March 8, 2027.

name: Keiki Construction Zone
schedule_text: Sunday, November 8, 2026, 9 AM-3 PM.
description: Family event with operating construction equipment, horseback riding and livestock, plus a farmers market, local vendors, food and live entertainment.
notes: Venue, organizer and admission not stated in the snippet I retrieved. Needs a follow-up before publishing.

name: Kimchi Festival Hawaiʻi (Kimchi Day Festival)
schedule_text: Annual one-day festival; 2026 edition Saturday, November 14, 2026, 10 AM-7 PM.
organizer: Kimchi Festival Hawaiʻi (earlier editions hosted by The United Korean Association of Hawaii)
description: Celebration of kimchi and Korean culture with kimchi tastings, food vendors, cultural performances and community activities. The 2026 edition is announced on the festival's own site.
source_label: Kimchi Festival Hawaii official site; Hawaii Parent November 2026 calendar
notes: The 2026 venue is not stated in the sources I found. Earlier editions were at Makiki District Park Field, 1527 Keeaumoku St (town side), so confirm before listing the venue. Free admission was reported for the 2024 edition only.

name: Korean Festival Hawaiʻi
schedule_text: Annual one-day festival in August. The 22nd edition was Saturday, August 8, 2026, 10am–8pm. Confirm the 2027 date with the organizer.
description: Korean cuisine, K-pop and traditional performances, fashion, art and family activities. Food vendors serve dishes such as kalbi, mandoo and kimchi.
notes: The festival moved back to Kapiʻolani Park in 2026. Older listings that point to Honolulu Hale are outdated. The admission and address details come from third-party event listings (makekemaps and The Creative City). A separate Taste of Korea event (see below) also exists.

name: Lei Day at Kapiʻolani Park
schedule_text: Annual; listing expects May 1, 2027. Date is described as expected, not confirmed.
description: Annual Lei Day festival listed as a vendor event on a vendor-events directory.
notes: Spring (May) is at the edge of your window. Date is expected only, and the source gives no vendor specifics for this event. Verify with the City or the organizer. Separate from the May Day Lei Day at Waimea Valley, which I did not research.

name: Mōʻiliʻili Summer Fest & Bon Dance
schedule_text: Annual summer event. The 13th edition was held July 4, 2026.
description: Honolulu Magazine calls it Honolulu's largest and arguably most popular bon dance.
notes: The sources give no venue, hours or vendor details. The Creative City calendar lists it as '13th Annual Moiliili Summer Fest & Bon Dance'.

name: Nā Lehua Marketplace & Festival
venue_name: Hawaiʻi Convention Center, ground-floor Kamehameha Exhibit Halls
schedule_text: Three days, Friday through Sunday, November 6-8, 2026. Daily hours not stated in source.
description: New marketplace and festival with hundreds of local vendors, live entertainment and island-inspired products, per the Convention Center's announcement as reported by a travel guide.
source_label: Hawaii-guide.com holiday craft fair season guide (third-party, citing HCC announcement)
notes: Ticket-sale details were listed as due in fall, so admission is unknown. Debuting in 2026. Not the same event as Made in Hawaii Festival. Food vendors are not specifically confirmed; the source says 'vendors' and 'island-inspired products'. Check the HCC site for details.

name: Obon Celebration at Hawaiʻi's Plantation Village
schedule_text: Annual obon celebration that opened the 2026 bon season on June 6, 2026 (36th annual).
description: Bon dancing under the stars, local food offerings and a pop-up craft tent.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, with The Creative City calendar for the '36th Annual' label
notes: The venue's own page was not retrieved, so the address, hours and admission are null.

name: Okinawan FEASTival
venue_name: Okinawan-owned restaurants and food businesses across Oʻahu
schedule_text: A two-week run of restaurant specials after the Okinawan Festival. The 2026 run was September 7–21 per the organizer's current notice.
description: Restaurants and food businesses owned by Okinawans offer special Okinawan dishes and deals. The aim is to help people discover and keep supporting these eateries.
notes: The same page also shows a line reading 'November 2 - 8', which conflicts with September 7–21 and is probably a leftover from another year. The list of participating restaurants was not captured.

name: Okinawan Festival
schedule_text: Annual festival around Labor Day weekend, run by the Hawaiʻi United Okinawa Association. The 44th edition was held September 5–6, 2026. Check okinawanfestival.com for the 2027 dates.
description: Okinawan food (soba, andagi), music, martial arts and performing arts, craft vendors and cultural exhibits. The 2026 edition was scaled down because of Convention Center renovations, with no bon dance or early admission. A shuttle ran from the Civic Center lot, with a $5 return ticket.
notes: The organizer's site lists Sunday 10am–4pm. The Saturday 10am–5pm time comes from a third-party listing (mygoldscene). HUOA is based at 94-587 Ukeʻe St, Waipahu. 2027 dates were not found.

name: Pan-Pacific Festival
venue_name: Multiple venues from Ala Moana Center to Waikīkī; Kalākaua Ave for the Hoʻolauleʻa
schedule_text: Usually the second weekend of June. The Hoʻolauleʻa block party is on Friday and the parade on Sunday. The 44th festival is June 11–13, 2027.
organizer: Pan-Pacific Festival Foundation and the Matsuri in Hawaiʻi Committee
description: Japanese and Pacific cultural festival with a Hoʻolauleʻa street party, a parade and performances. The 2026 edition (June 12–14) also included a bon dance on Kalākaua Ave on June 12.
notes: The organizer says dates are subject to change. Honolulu Magazine's bon dance list gives the handle @panpacificfestival but doesn't say which platform.

name: Punahou Carnival 2027: Party Like It's 2000
schedule_text: Two days, Friday February 5 and Saturday February 6, 2027, 11 AM-10 PM.
description: Punahou's annual financial-aid fundraiser carnival with food booths (including the famous malasadas), a large art gallery of Hawaiʻi artists, rides, games, a silent auction and live music.
source_label: Punahou School carnival page; Punahou Bulletin (Oct 20, 2026) confirms Feb 5-6 dates
notes: Food booths are school-run rather than independent vendors, but the carnival has a large art gallery of Hawaiʻi artists. Admission to the 2026 carnival was reported free (KITV); 2027 admission not stated. The Instagram handle comes from a Honolulu Magazine guide to the 2026 carnival.

name: Taste of Korea in Honolulu
schedule_text: A one-day event listed for Saturday, May 16, 2026, 10am–3pm. Whether it repeats in 2027 is unconfirmed.
description: Korean food and culture event listed on an events aggregator.
notes: A single third-party mention. No organizer page was found.

name: The East Honolulu Food Festival
schedule_text: Listed under May 2027 with no confirmed date.
description: A food festival named in an Oʻahu events calendar for May 2027.
notes: Name and month only. The 'east' side is inferred from the event name. I did not find the organizer, venue or date.

name: Waikīkī SPAM JAM
schedule_text: Annual block party. The 2027 date is Saturday, April 24, 4:00–10:00pm. Participating restaurants run a Dine-In SPAM event April 17–May 2, 2027.
description: Food festival built around Spam dishes such as nachos, manapua and gelato. The 2026 edition had more than 40 food and retail booths. It is a fundraiser for the Hawaiʻi Foodbank, with donation tents on site.
notes: The source page does not give the street or venue for the block party.

name: We Are Samoa Festival
schedule_text: Listed on a third-party calendar for April 21–29, 2027.
description: A Samoan cultural festival named in an Oʻahu events calendar for April 2027.
notes: Name and date range only. I did not find the organizer's page, the venue or whether it includes food vendors.

name: East Side Underground Market
schedule_text: Typically the first Saturday of every month, 4 to 9 p.m. (per Honolulu Magazine).
description: Monthly evening market listed among O‘ahu's vintage shopping events.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Shop Vintage on Oʻahu This Summer' (2026)
notes: Third-party listing. Whether it continues past summer 2026 is unconfirmed. Not the same as Koko Marina Makers Market, which is already in the directory. Kind chosen as flea_market because the source groups it with vintage markets.

name: Free Parking Flea Market
venue_name: The Barn at SALT at Our Kakaʻako
schedule_text: Evening flea market on select dates. The summer 2026 edition was listed as August, date TBD, 5 to 10 p.m.
description: Evening flea market of vintage vendors and local small businesses, with local food vendors and live DJ sets.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Shop Vintage on Oʻahu This Summer' (2026)
notes: No exact 2026 date was stated in the source. SALT's event pages I found were for 2025 editions. Check @freeparkingfleamarket for the next date. Separate from Makia Market, which is already in the directory.

name: Harbors Vintage Market
schedule_text: Periodic Saturday vintage markets from 3 to 7 p.m. 2026 dates listed: August 15 and September 12.
description: The two-story vintage shop becomes a market with vintage vendors and local businesses, selling clothing, accessories and collectibles.
source_label: Honolulu Magazine, 'Where to Shop Vintage on Oʻahu This Summer' (2026)
notes: Third-party listing; I did not verify against the organizer's own page. Both dates have already passed. Check the shop's site or Instagram for later dates.

name: Wiki Wiki One Day Vintage Collectibles & Hawaiiana Show
venue_name: Neal S. Blaisdell Center (Galleria and Hawaiʻi Suites)
schedule_text: A few one-day shows per year, usually on a Sunday. Regular shopping hours 11 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. 2026 dates: March 22, July 19, October 4, November 22.
admission: $6 general admission; free for two kids 12 and under with each paid adult ticket
description: Vintage collectibles and Hawaiiana show with 100+ vendor tables. Vendors come from the outer islands, Oʻahu, Japan and the U.S. mainland.
source_label: Organizer Instagram bio (2026 dates), corroborated by Aloha State Daily 2026-09-21 and Blaisdell Center events calendar
notes: Mar 22 and Oct 4 times come from the Blaisdell Center listing. Nov 22 times assume the 'regular shopping hours' stated in the Aloha State Daily article. The July 19 time was not confirmed (a third-party listing showed a different window), so it is null. Early entry was 10:00 a.m. for the Mar 22 and Oct 4 shows. Oct 4 has already happened.

name: Mele Market at Pearl at Kalauao
schedule_text: Listed for December 2026 with the date still to be confirmed.
description: Holiday 'Mele Market' listed for December 2026 at Pearl at Kalauao.
notes: Title-only listing. The venue comes from the event name. It may be a holiday edition of the Night Market at Pearl at Kalauao on your skip list; check for duplication. Vendor types not stated.

name: Annual Unthirsty Plant Sale (Hālawa Xeriscape Garden)
schedule_text: Annual sale, typically early August. The 2026 sale was Saturday Aug 1, 9am-1pm. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
organizer: Honolulu Board of Water Supply, co-sponsored by Friends of Hālawa Xeriscape Garden
admission: Free admission; free street parking and a shuttle on Iwaena Street. Payments by major credit card only (no cash).
description: Drought-tolerant and native plants from local vendors, with agency and community booths, mini-workshops, a rain barrel giveaway, a Cactus & Succulent Society of Hawaiʻi display, and a UH Master Gardener Plant Doctors booth.
source_label: Honolulu Board of Water Supply (organizer page)
notes: This event has already happened. The Honolulu Orchid Society also staffed an orchid-care booth, per a KHON story dated 2026-07-25. The central side tag is my reading of the Hālawa location, and the source does not give a city or ZIP. The Friends of Hālawa Xeriscape Garden offer a membership with 10% off plant purchases.

name: Ewa Orchid Society Orchid Show and Plant Sale
schedule_text: Annual show. The 2026 show was Friday July 17 and Saturday July 18. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
description: Orchid show and plant sale with blooming orchid plants and show trophies. The Honolulu Orchid Society exhibited a display there.
source_label: Honolulu Orchid Society August 2026 newsletter (wrap-up of the Ewa show)
notes: This event has already happened. Only an indirect wrap-up was found, and the extracted text did not show the venue. Venue, address, hours and admission are null. Check the Ewa Orchid Society's own site for the 2027 show.

name: Honolulu Orchid Society Orchid Show & Plant Sale (87th Annual, "Orchids Spooktacular")
schedule_text: Annual show, held on a Friday and Saturday in October. The 2026 show was Oct 9-10, 9am-4pm both days. The plant sale closed at 3pm on Saturday. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
description: Orchid displays by the Honolulu Orchid Society and guest societies, a plant sale by island nurseries, a country store, free orchid workshops, a plant doctor, and UH CTAHR and HDOA information tables.
notes: This event has already happened as of 2026-10-31. Other sources: AOS calendar says no AOS judging; Hoodline article dated 2026-10-05. Plant sale hours are 9-4 Friday and 9-3 Saturday. Neighborhood not stated in the sources.

name: Kunia Orchid Society 68th Orchid Show & Plant Sale
schedule_text: Two-day annual show. The 2026 show ran Friday March 20 and Saturday March 21, theme "March Madness". The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
description: Orchid show and plant sale held in the Leilehua High School gym by the Kunia Orchid Society.
source_label: Honolulu Orchid Society events calendar (listing for a sister society's show)
notes: This event has already happened. The 9am-5pm time is the one the listing shows for March 20. Saturday hours were not stated. Kunia Orchid Society is also listed as a guest society on the HOS show page. Check the Kunia Orchid Society's own page for the 2027 date.

name: Lyon Arboretum Fall Plant & Craft Sale
venue_name: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum (surrounding the Visitor Center and Greenhouse)
schedule_text: Friday Dec 4 and Saturday Dec 5, 2026, 9 AM to 3 PM each day
organizer: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
description: Fall plant and craft sale at Lyon Arboretum in Mānoa Valley with local vendors, music and food. Plants include tropical ornamentals, Hoya, natives, ferns, orchids, jade vines, aroids, gingers, bromeliads and carnivorous plants from Lyon's Horticulture Dept., Hui Ku Maoli Ola, Laʻau Hawaiʻi, Olomana Tropicals, Lang's Nursery, Mix Plate Nurseries, Nuʻuanu Orchids and others. Also aloha shirts, local honey and art. Proceeds support Lyon Arboretum's conservation, education and research.
notes: Page indicates a vehicle-based parking reservation system (one reservation per vehicle). Reservation booking date and admission price were cut off in the retrieved text, so verify on the organizer page. Street address not stated in the source.

name: Lyon Arboretum Spring Plant & Craft Sale
venue_name: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum (around the Visitor Center and greenhouse)
schedule_text: Annual spring sale in May. The 2026 sale was Friday May 8 and Saturday May 9, 9am to 3pm each day. Walk-ups without reservations were admitted from 10:30am.
organizer: Harold L. Lyon Arboretum, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
description: Spring plant and craft sale with tropical ornamentals, native plants, orchids, begonias, hoyas, ferns and exotic edibles, plus handmade goods.
source_label: Hawaiʻi Public Radio community calendar (Lyon Arboretum listing)
notes: This event has already happened. Parking reservations were via Eventbrite, opening April 13, 2026. A 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.

name: Waimea Valley Nursery Saturday Plant Sale
schedule_text: Every Saturday, 8 AM to 12 PM, through December 27, 2026 (listing span May 24 to December 27, 2026)
description: Weekly plant sale at the Waimea Valley Nursery with a variety of plants for home and garden, including fruiting and flowering plants, native trees and easy-care greenery.
source_label: North Shore Chamber of Commerce event listing via Business Daily Network
notes: Third-party chamber listing; the listed start date (May 24, 2026) is a Sunday, so confirm the Saturday schedule with Waimea Valley. Organizer and admission not stated in the listing. No individual dates listed because the source gives a recurring range only.

name: Windward Orchid Society 44th Annual Orchid Show & Plant Sale
schedule_text: Three-day annual show. The 2026 show ran Friday March 20 through Sunday March 22, theme "Stars of the Show Orchids Galore". Plant sales closed at 2pm on Sunday. The 2027 date has not been announced in the sources found.
description: Annual orchid show and plant sale run by the Windward Orchid Society in the S.W. King Intermediate cafeteria.
source_label: Honolulu Orchid Society events calendar (listing for a sister society's show)
notes: This event has already happened. The 10am-5pm time is the one the listing shows for March 20. Saturday and Sunday hours were not stated, and the Saturday date is implied by the three-day run. Check the Windward Orchid Society's own page for the 2027 date.

name: Kailua Swap Meet
venue_name: Emmanuel Episcopal Church (per Facebook page; earlier editions at Aikahi Elementary School)
schedule_text: Irregular community swap meet. The Facebook page showed a June 6 post (year not shown) with hours 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m.
description: Community swap meet with craft, food and garage-sale vendors. The 2023 edition at Aikahi Elementary drew 100+ vendors.
notes: The organizer website only shows a July 2023 event. The Facebook post's year was not visible, so I could not confirm a 2026 date. The page's intro lists 281 Ilihau St, which is Aikahi Elementary's address, so I left the address null because the current venue's street address was not found. Verify before publishing.
